text:
zoe: quick triage note — running into intermittent SSE parse failures in sampleapp-web when auth refresh happens mid-stream. repro is pretty small: start stream, force token rotate, tiny network blip, reconnect. Browser fetch path, sdk@0.9.3.

mike: can you paste the raw curl -v -N capture?

zoe: sure. masked creds. trimmed:

```
$ curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <tok>" "https://staging.redwood.io/s/stream"
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< Content-Type: text/event-stream
< Transfer-Encoding: chunked
: keepalive
data: {"id":"x1","msg":"hi"}

\r\n{"id":"x2","msg":"there"}

```

zoe: the problematic case is when that leading CRLF ("\r\n") or sometimes a stray 0x00 byte lands between chunks and the client parser treats it as continuation of previous data. our parser then does JSON.parse on a malformed string and throws.

oliver: which parser variant? EventSource polyfill or fetch-stream?

zoe: fetch-stream in the JS SDK. current logic: append incoming bytes to buffer, find "\n\n" boundaries, for each event split lines, concat lines that start with 'data:' and JSON.parse the result. no CRLF normalization and we keep partial buffers across aborts.

mike: sounds like a combo bug: proxy/edge coalescing + client not clearing state on abort -> partials get stitched. two immediate mitigations: normalize CRLF to LF on incoming bytes, and clear partial buffer synchronously when abort() is called. also ignore lines that start with ':' (keepalives).

oliver: agree. Add a conservative repair: if JSON.parse fails, try trimming leading non-printable chars (^[\x00-\x1F]+) and retry once — emit a metric when we do this so we can monitor masking.

zoe: implemented a small patch locally: buffer = buffer.replace(/\r\n/g, "\n"); onAbort() { partial = '' } ; parse path only JSON.parse on lines after trimming and only if line starts with 'data:'. Quick stress: 10k flapper iterations, failures from ~6% -> ~0.4%. still seeing rare fails when refresh+keepalive align within ~15-30ms.

mike: we should also harden reconnect timing: don't reconnect immediately in the same microtask — clear buffers, then setTimeout(reconnect, 0). that reduces risk of V8 reusing internal buffers and merging.

oliver: double-check edge: what are we running? traefik / envoy? some proxies (haproxy/nginx) may coalesce TCP writes or re-chunk when Transfer-Encoding: chunked is proxied. we should test with proxy buffering off for streaming routes.

zoe: staging is behind ALB -> traefik. I'll flip streaming buffering off for that route and re-run the harness.

mike: also add SDK metric parse_error{repair_mode=trim} and parse_error{original_throw=true} to differentiate repaired vs unrepaired. tag with near_refresh=true if within X ms of an auth refresh.

z oe: (typo) zoe: i'll add metric and unit tests: simulate CRLF split, leading NUL, and abort+immediate reconnect. will open PR.

ci-bot: branch fix/sse-boundary-robustness CI checks started.

ci-bot: build passed for fix/sse-boundary-robustness (CI: 10/10) :white_check_mark:

mike: after PR lands, backport to 0.9.x patch and add a line in changelog + sampleapp README showing how to curl -v -N and what to look for ("look for explicit CRLF or 0x00 between events"). mark as P2 because unguarded consumers might crash.

oliver: follow-up: I'll spin up a local envoy with identical routing and tcpdump to see if the 0x00 / CRLF is introduced by our edge. if it's server-side we should consider emitting an explicit blank 'data:\n\n' separator after each event for a few releases. heavier but safer.

zoe: agreed — conservative client fixes + metrics first. PR link in thread (private). will monitor metric post-deploy and escalate if >0.2% parse_error in the next 24h.

mike: one more small note: add defensive try/catch in sampleapp example code to avoid apps crashing (show recommended wrapper).

zoe: ack. leaving repro gist here: https://gist.github.com/redwood/devex-sse-auth-flip (internal). thanks all.
